summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly, with vector search emerging as a native data type rather than a separate database category. By 2026, an estimated 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search, driving PostgreSQL and other multimodel databases to become ascendant while purpose-built vector databases like Pinecone and Milvus narrow to high-performance niches. Platforms like Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, and Databricks Mosaic AI now integrate LLM inference, embeddings, and RAG workflows alongside traditional analytics on unified, governed platforms.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs (from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, OpenAI, and others) via SQL and Python functions for tasks like summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and text completion. Cortex Search delivers hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval for RAG, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language querying of structured data. Snowflake Postgres further unifies the popular database with analytics and AI on a single secure platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake offers a built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY and related functions, plus Cortex Search for managed vector/hybrid retrieval. No third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs via Cortex (Claude, Llama, Mistral, GPT models, Snowflake Arctic) callable directly in SQL/Python; Cortex Agents for agentic workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by compute and per-token/per-function usage for Cortex LLM functions. No separate upfront license; costs scale with query and inference volume.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration and BigQuery vector search
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, and more) using SQL directly in the data warehouse. It integrates with Vertex AI for generative AI, remote model inference, and embeddings, and supports BigQuery Graph for relationship analysis plus vector, text, and hybrid search for RAG and context-retrieval applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides built-in VECTOR_SEARCH functions and vector indexes for embeddings-based semantic and hybrid search without external tooling.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI (Gemini and PaLM models) for generative tasks, ML.GENERATE_TEXT, and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions callable in SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go: on-demand bytes-processed pricing or capacity-based (slots) for queries; ML/AI model creation and inference incur additional compute charges, and Vertex AI inference is billed separately.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL extends into AI via pgvector, which adds a vector data type with indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat) for high-dimensional embedding storage and similarity search directly in the database. The pgai extension brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL. PostgreSQL is described as 'ascendant' as vectors become a data type in existing multimodel databases rather than requiring a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension (native when installed). Core PostgreSQL does not include vector search; it is enabled by the open-source pgvector extension, which is bundled/available in most managed PostgreSQL offerings. Considered first-class in the PostgreSQL ecosystem but technically an extension.
databases.llm_integration: pgai enables calling external LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) from SQL for embedding generation and RAG; no built-in hosted models in core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on hosting (self-managed or managed providers like Timescale, Supabase, AWS RDS/Aurora, Azure). External LLM API calls billed by the provider.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL integration with SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by calling out to Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock (for generative AI and embeddings) and Amazon Comprehend (for sentiment analysis). It surfaces ML inference as SQL functions, minimizing data movement between the database and ML services.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only through the pgvector extension, not as a built-in Aurora ML capability. Aurora ML focuses on invoking external inference, so native vector search is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for foundation-model inference and embeddings invoked via SQL functions; SageMaker for custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself beyond standard Aurora instance/storage/I-O costs; you pay separately for SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend usage invoked.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL with SageMaker/Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL statements, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database prediction functions and integration with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and large language model inference on warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML does not provide built-in vector similarity search; vector/embedding workflows require external services or other tools. Marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference callable from SQL and SageMaker for custom and foundation models.
databases.pricing_notes: Model training incurs SageMaker costs (or is included up to limits for certain model types); predictions run within Redshift compute. Standard Redshift node/serverless pricing applies plus any external inference charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides a full generative AI stack — model fine-tuning, foundation model APIs, model serving, agent frameworks, and evaluation — on the lakehouse. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector database integrated with Unity Catalog for governed embeddings, automatic sync from Delta tables, and RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector index with automatic synchronization from Delta tables and governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to open and proprietary LLMs (Llama, DBRX, and external models like OpenAI/Anthropic) plus fine-tuning and agent orchestration.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed by compute/endpoint usage, with pay-per-token options for Foundation Model APIs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic search and RAG on operational data
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing and querying high-dimensional embeddings alongside operational JSON documents, supporting semantic search, hybrid search, and RAG directly on live application data. It integrates with the Atlas aggregation pipeline, making vectors a native part of the document model rather than a separate store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of the Atlas managed platform using $vectorSearch in the aggregation pipeline with dedicated vector indexes (HNSW). No third-party extension needed.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted in-database LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of MongoDB Atlas; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes with pricing based on dedicated search node compute/storage or included within cluster resources depending on tier.
